questions.text: An interior column (not exposed) has primary reinforcement of 28 mm diameter bars. What is the minimum concrete cover?

rationale.a: Unlike precast, cast-in-place columns use fixed values rather than bar diameters.
rationale.b: 20 mm is for interior slabs and walls.
rationale.d: 50 mm is for weather-exposed large bars.
rationale.correct: For nonprestressed concrete not exposed to weather, the specified cover for primary reinforcement in beams and columns is a fixed 40 mm (§ 420.6.1.1).

questions.text: A cantilever balcony spandrel is exposed to weather. Primary reinforcing bars are 20 mm diameter. What minimum concrete cover applies?

rationale.a: 40 mm applies to weather-exposed bars 16 mm or smaller.
rationale.c: 75 mm is only for concrete cast directly against earth.
rationale.d: 30 mm is below the minimum requirement for weather exposure in cast-in-place concrete.
rationale.correct: For concrete exposed to earth or weather, 50 mm cover is required for bars 20 mm through 58 mm in diameter (NSCP 2015 § 420.6.1.1).
rationale.takeaway: Weather exposed: Bars ≥ 20 mm = 50 mm; Bars ≤ 16 mm = 40 mm.

questions.text: A prestressed hollow-core slab is installed indoors in a climate-controlled office building (fully enclosed, not exposed to weather or soil). What is the minimum cover to the prestressing strand?

rationale.b: 40 mm is required for prestressed beams and columns principal reinforcement, not slabs.
rationale.c: 50 mm is for prestressed members exposed to weather or soil.
rationale.d: 75 mm is for concrete cast directly against earth.
rationale.correct: Per NSCP 2015 § 420.6.1.3, prestressed concrete slabs, walls, and joists not exposed to weather or in contact with ground require a minimum cover of 20 mm.

questions.text: A precast wall panel (not exposed) has 32 mm diameter bars. What is the minimum cover per NSCP?

rationale.d: Bar diameter is only used as a cover calculation for precast beams/columns.
rationale.correct: Precast nonprestressed slabs and walls not exposed to weather require 15 mm cover for bars 32 mm or smaller (§ 420.6.1.2).
rationale.takeaway: Precast unexposed Slabs/Walls (≤32 mm bars) = 15 mm.

questions.text: What is the minimum concrete cover for reinforcement in a spread footing cast directly against earth?

rationale.a: 40 mm is for interior beams and columns.
rationale.b: 50 mm is for weather-exposed reinforcement of large diameters.
rationale.d: 100 mm exceeds the minimum requirement specified by the code.
rationale.correct: 75 mm is the required minimum cover for all reinforcement in concrete cast against and permanently in contact with earth (NSCP 2015 § 420.6.1.1). This provides maximum protection against corrosion from soil moisture.

questions.text: An exposed weather-facing wall uses 12 mm diameter bars. Per NSCP, what is the minimum cover?

rationale.b: 50 mm is for bars 20 mm and larger.
rationale.d: 30 mm is not an NSCP specified value for this condition.
rationale.correct: Concrete exposed to earth or weather requires 40 mm cover for bars 16 mm or smaller (§ 420.6.1.1).

questions.text: In a code review, an engineer specifies 35 mm cover for an interior precast beam with 25 mm diameter bars. Is this compliant, and what is the minimum required cover?

options.text: Compliant; 35 mm is acceptable as it provides sufficient protection against corrosion and fire exposure
Non-compliant; minimum is 25 mm (bar diameter), which is the standard for ensuring structural integrity and durability
Compliant; exceeds absolute minimum of 15 mm, which is typically used for non-structural elements
Compliant; 35 mm exceeds the minimum of 25 mm (bar diameter) but is within the 15–40 mm range per NSCP 2015.

rationale.a: Correct but incomplete logic regarding the $d_b$ rule.
rationale.b: 35 mm is compliant because it is *more* than the 25 mm minimum.
rationale.c: The absolute minimum for a beam is $d_b$ (25 mm), not 15 mm (which is for slabs).
rationale.correct: Per § 420.6.1.2, interior precast beams use $d_b$ as the minimum (min 15 mm, max 40 mm). For a 25 mm bar, the code minimum is 25 mm. A specification of 35 mm is compliant as it exceeds the minimum and falls within the allowable envelope.

questions.text: Compare the minimum cover for a 20 mm diameter primary bar in an interior beam: cast-in-place vs. precast concrete.

options.text: Cast-in-place 40 mm; Precast 20 mm, ensuring adequate protection against environmental factors
Cast-in-place 40 mm; Precast db (min 15, max 40 mm) = 20 mm
Both require 40 mm, providing uniformity in structural protection across different construction methods
Cast-in-place 20 mm; Precast 40 mm, which may vary based on specific project requirements

rationale.a: While the values are correct, option (b) correctly identifies the logic for the precast calculation.
rationale.c: Precast concrete benefits from lower cover requirements due to factory-controlled quality.
rationale.d: Cast-in-place requires higher cover than precast for interior beams.
rationale.correct: Interior cast-in-place beams require 40 mm cover (§ 420.6.1.1). Interior precast beams/columns allow cover equal to the nominal bar diameter ($d_b$), but not less than 15 mm and need not exceed 40 mm (§ 420.6.1.2). For a 20 mm bar, $d_b = 20	ext{ mm}$.

questions.text: A prestressed concrete beam is exposed to weather. What is the minimum cover to the prestressing strand?

rationale.a: 25 mm is for prestressed slabs, walls, or joists exposed to weather.
rationale.c: 50 mm is required for reinforced (nonprestressed) concrete with large bars, but not for prestressed beams.
rationale.d: 75 mm is for concrete cast against earth.
rationale.correct: Per NSCP 2015 § 420.6.1.3, prestressed members exposed to weather or soil require 40 mm cover for 'other members' (including beams and columns).
rationale.takeaway: Prestressed exposed: Slabs/Walls = 25 mm; Other members = 40 mm.

questions.text: An interior floor slab (not exposed to weather) uses 16 mm diameter bars. What is the minimum cover requirement?

rationale.a: 15 mm is the minimum for precast slabs/walls, not cast-in-place.
rationale.c: 25 mm is not a standard minimum for unexposed reinforced concrete slabs.
rationale.d: 40 mm is the requirement for interior beams and columns.
rationale.correct: 20 mm is the minimum cover for non-exposed slabs, walls, and joists with bar diameters of 32 mm or smaller (NSCP 2015 § 420.6.1.1).
